2608.18631.title: Preference Reasoning under Indeterminacy in Large Language Models
2608.18631.paper_summary: As large language models evolve into decision-making agents, the ability to reason over preferences becomes fundamental to alignment, coordination, and collective intelligence. Yet, unlike standard benchmarks, real-world preference reasoning is inherently indeterminate: information may be incomplete, and valid solutions may not exist. We argue that indeterminacy, rather than correctness alone, is a central challenge for AI reasoning. We formalize this challenge along two axes, (i) epistemic indeterminacy, arising from incomplete, partial, or expressive preferences, and (ii) structural indeterminacy, arising from the non-existence of solutions under standard social choice concepts. Across a hierarchy of tasks, we show that state-of-the-art language models systematically fail to distinguish between determined and undetermined instances, exhibiting miscalibrated reasoning even in verification settings.
2608.18631.paper_summary_zh: 隨著大型語言模型演變為決策代理，對偏好的推理能力成為對齊、協調和集體智慧的基礎。<lb/>然而，與標準基準不同，現實世界的偏好推理本質上是非確定的：信息可能不完整，且有效解決方案可能不存在。<lb/>我們認為，非確定性，而非僅僅是正確性，是人工智慧推理的一個核心挑戰。<lb/>我們沿著兩個軸對這一挑戰進行形式化，(i) 認識論非確定性，源於不完整、部分或表達性偏好，以及 (ii) 結構性非確定性，源於在標準社會選擇概念下解決方案的不存在。<lb/>在一系列任務中，我們顯示最先進的語言模型系統性地無法區分確定和不確定的實例，即使在驗證環境中也表現出錯誤的推理。
